title: Redwood PLG Quickstart Discovery - Borealis AI
summary: Introductory PLG quickstart discovery. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private; primary interest in fast time-to-first-token, free credits for experimentation, and security (SOC2, VPC/KMS). Agreed next steps: send pricing and security docs, provide quickstart guide + test account, and run a short benchmark with their prompt set.
next_steps: Jordan to send pricing and Redwood security pack (SOC2, ISO summary) by 2026-02-19
Priya to share quickstart guide + sample notebook and invite to Redwood free credits program
Customer to provide small prompt set and SLA targets for benchmark by 2026-02-23
Schedule 30m benchmark check-in for week of 2026-02-23
action_items: Jordan Lee: Send pricing and security docs; due 2026-02-19
Priya Natarajan: Share quickstart + sample notebook and create free credits invite; due 2026-02-18
Maya Chen: Share prompt set and desired latency/throughput targets; due 2026-02-23
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood. Quick intro from us, then want to hear about your goals for evaluation.
[00:15] Maya Chen: Hi, Maya here. CTO at Borealis. Appreciate it. We're exploring hosted vs dedicated or a private deployment, mainly to power an internal search and question-answering layer for our analytics product.
[00:30] Luis Ortega: Yeah hi, Luis, ML eng. Main things for us: quick integration, low friction for product teams, and we want to understand time-to-first-token with your quickstart and free credits.
[00:45] Jordan Lee: totally. On the PLG side our quickstart is designed for exactly that — free credits, example notebooks, and an SDK so teams can get to first token in minutes. Priya will walk through the quickstart flow.
[01:05] Priya Natarajan: Thanks Jordan. I'll share my screen after intros, but high level: hosted API is easiest — self-serve keys, per-token billing; Dedicated is reserved capacity for predictable throughput; Private is VPC/on-prem for regulated needs.
[01:30] Samir Patel: For us, the security bar is pretty high. SOC2 is table stakes, and we use SSO/SAML, and keys in KMS. If you offer Private we'd need to know about HSM/KMS integrations and audit logs.
[01:50] Priya Natarajan: Understood. We support SOC2 controls, SSO (SAML/OIDC), and can integrate with customer KMS for Private. Audit logs and per-request tracing are available in Redwood Console.
[02:10] Maya Chen: Good. Another concern is latency - we have latency SLOs of < 200ms for short prompts. How does hosted compare to Dedicated in practice?
[02:25] Priya Natarajan: Good question. Hosted can be very fast for bursty workloads; we have curated model profiles with measured p95 latencies. Dedicated gives you reserved GPUs and lower variance for sustained traffic. We often recommend starting hosted for POC quickstarts to validate quality and then move to Dedicated for production.
[02:50] Luis Ortega: And Private for data residency? We have some datasets that can't leave our VPC.
[03:00] Jordan Lee: Exactly. Private gives a customer-managed control plane and you can keep tokens/local KV cache in your network. That said Private onboarding takes longer than the quickstart.
[03:15] Priya Natarajan: If I can jump in, for the quickstart we provide a sample notebook that shows API key creation, a small prompt set, and a benchmark script. In our experience teams can generate first token in under 10 minutes if they follow the notebook.
[03:35] Maya Chen: That matches what we want. Free credits are important so the product teams can experiment without procurement. How big are the credits?
[03:45] Jordan Lee: We typically offer an evaluation credit package that covers a couple of thousand generation tokens and some embedding ops — enough to run multiple experiments. I'll confirm the exact amount in the follow-up.
[03:58] Luis Ortega: Could you also share any guidance on batching and quantization? We run both embeddings and chat-style completions.
[04:10] Priya Natarajan: Yes — Redwood Optimize will suggest batching and quantization profiles for your workload. For embeddings we often batch to improve throughput; for latency-sensitive chat we'll use smaller batches and KV cache. Also model quantization can reduce cost but may impact output quality, we can recommend configs.
[04:35] Maya Chen: Who on our side would be the right contact to do the benchmark? Luis probably.
[04:40] Luis Ortega: Yep I can run the prompt set and report latency and cost.
[04:48] Jordan Lee: Great. Quick qualification: are you evaluating any other providers?
[04:55] Maya Chen: We're also running quick experiments with OpenAI and looking at Anthropic for safety features; there's some internal discussion about using SageMaker endpoints for very large batch jobs.
[05:08] Priya Natarajan: Good to know. Our differentiator is production-grade serving with clear levers for cost vs latency and native rollout tooling. Also the same API across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
[05:25] Samir Patel: On compliance, can you share how logs and audits work? We need immutable audit trails and retention policies.
[05:35] Priya Natarajan: For Hosted we provide tenant-level audit logs with configurable retention; Dedicated/Private can ship logs to your SIEM or S3 within your control plane. We support encryption-at-rest and KMS integration.
[05:55] Maya Chen: Do you have any published perf numbers for models at different sequence lengths?
[06:05] Priya Natarajan: We publish model profiles — p50/p95 token latencies under sample hardware configs. We'll share the performance profile deck. Note sometimes our automatic transcription of docs mixes up names, but the profiles are concrete.
[06:25] Luis Ortega: For integration, what SDKs do you have? Node and Python are critical for us.
[06:32] Jordan Lee: We support Node, Python, and HTTP REST. We also have examples for TypeScript, and a serverless quickstart.
[06:45] Maya Chen: About pricing — we need both per-token pricing for Hosted and committed pricing for Dedicated. Also do you provide a minimum commitment?
[06:58] Jordan Lee: Hosted is pay-as-you-go. Dedicated is monthly reserved capacity; minimums depend on GPU class and region — I'll include a sample pricing sheet in the follow-up. For pilots teams often start Hosted and then talk about a Dedicated commitment once they have predictable usage.
[07:20] Luis Ortega: Any gotchas when moving from Hosted to Dedicated in terms of model versions, or will rollouts be seamless?
[07:30] Priya Natarajan: Rollouts are config-level; you can pin model versions and rollout policies are consistent. We also support automatic fallback to compatible variants if a model isn't available in a region.
[07:45] Jordan Lee: Let's talk about the actual quickstart flow — Priya?
[07:50] Priya Natarajan: Sure. Step 1: sign up for a free account and get free credits. Step 2: follow the notebook; create API key in Console. Step 3: run sample prompts and then run the benchmark script with your prompt set. We'll provide a sandbox project and a sample dashboard.
[08:10] Maya Chen: How long does it take to provision a sandbox?
[08:15] Priya Natarajan: For hosted sandbox it's immediate, you get API key and credits. For Dedicated trial provisioning can be a few days; Private requires more setup and security review.
[08:30] Luis Ortega: If we hit the free credits limit, can we top up immediately or do we need procurement?
[08:36] Jordan Lee: You can self-serve a payment method on Hosted to top up, but we'll also give a bumped evaluation if you're actively testing. We'll coordinate with you so you don't get blocked.
[08:50] Samir Patel: On the topic of data, request-level retention — can you control log retention and disable storage for certain calls?
[08:58] Priya Natarajan: Yes — we have controls for data retention per-tenant; for Private you keep all data in your environment. For Hosted we can set retention policies and have opt-out configs for specific routes.
[09:15] Maya Chen: Let's get a little technical. Luis: our prompts are fairly short, median 80 tokens, some few-shot examples up to 300 tokens. We expect peak concurrent requests of ~120 qps for embeddings batch jobs overnight and 400 rps for chat during business hours.
[09:40] Luis Ortega: We'll likely run embeddings as large batches overnight.
[09:45] Priya Natarajan: For that profile we might recommend Dedicated with configured autoscaling and burst capacity for day spikes. The Optimize toolkit will give batching suggestions and model choices that balance cost.
[09:58] Jordan Lee: Do you have regional constraints?
[10:02] Maya Chen: We operate primarily in NA and EU; data residency in EU is a preference for EU customers.
[10:10] Priya Natarajan: We have regions in NA and EU; for Private we can deploy in your VPC in the EU region.
[10:20] Jordan Lee: A couple of practical items: we'll send a security pack (SOC2, ISO summary, pen test summary) and a starter notebook. Priya will create the free credits invite and a sandbox project.
[10:35] Maya Chen: Sounds good. Any limitations on function-calling / tool-calling at early stages?
[10:42] Priya Natarajan: We support function/tool calling. For hosted, there's no functional limitation; for Private we can enable/disable connectors for data exfiltration protection.
[10:55] Luis Ortega: For cost estimation, does Redwood provide token-cost breakdowns by route/model?
[11:02] Priya Natarajan: Yes, Console shows token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route and model. You can also export CSVs for cost analysis.
[11:15] Samir Patel: Would you be willing to run a quick benchmark on our behalf if we provide the prompt set?
[11:22] Jordan Lee: We can run it jointly — Priya's team will help run a controlled benchmark and share results.
[11:30] Maya Chen: Great. Anything else from the Redwood side?
[11:34] Priya Natarajan: I'll note down the technical targets: <200ms for chat p95, embeddings throughput 120 qps overnight with batching. We'll propose model choices and quantization profiles.
[11:50] Luis Ortega: One more question — for integrations with our infra, do you provide a containerized connector or is everything via API?
[11:58] Priya Natarajan: For Private we can ship an on-prem package (containerized) and for Dedicated we have VPN/VPC peering options. Hosted is API-based.
[12:12] Jordan Lee: Ok let's recap next steps. Jordan to send pricing and security pack; Priya to create sandbox and free credits; Maya/Luis to share prompt set and SLA targets; plan to reconvene after benchmark.
[12:30] Maya Chen: Thanks, appreciated. We'll try to have the prompt set by next week.
[12:35] Samir Patel: Thanks everyone.
[12:38] Jordan Lee: Thanks, talk soon.
[12:45] [call ends]
